knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Two Matrices Are Conformable for Multiplication

question.:question/problem:
$A=\begin{bmatrix}9 & -3 & 7 \\ -5 & 0 & -5 \\ -6 & -1 & 8\end{bmatrix}$
$B=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 0 & -6 \\ -7 & 1 & 6\end{bmatrix}$
$C=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$
Which of the following statements are true regarding the matrices $A,B,$ and $C?$ Select all that apply. - **I.** The product $BA$ is well defined - **II.** The product $BC$ is well defined - **III.** The product $CB$ is well defined
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix, and $C$ is a $3\times 1$ column vector

There are $3$ columns in $B$ and $3$ rows in $A.$ Since the number of columns in $B$ equals the number of rows in $A,$ the matrices $B$ and $A$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
{B}_{2\times \boxed{\text{3}}}{\times }_{✓}{A}_{\boxed{\text{3}}\times 3}=\text{well defined}
$$

On the other hand, there are $3$ columns in $B$ and $3$ rows in $C.$ Since the number of columns in $B$ equals the number of rows in $C,$ the matrices $B$ and $C$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
{B}_{2\times \boxed{\text{3}}}{\times }_{✓}{C}_{\boxed{\text{3}}\times 1}=\text{well defined}
$$

Finally, there is $1$ column in $C$ and $2$ rows in $B.$ Since the number of columns in $C$ does **not** equal the number of rows in $B,$ the matrices $C$ and $B$ are **not** conformable for multiplication:

$$
{C}_{3\times 1}{\times }_{\ne }{B}_{2\times 3}=\text{undefined}
$$

Therefore, statements I and II are true, while statement III is false.
